mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% in the month prior to the decision point reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the preceding 60-day high-rate period (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS (monthly payrolls) coincides with stronger consumer confidence, which amplifies corporate hiring intentions and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 130,000 in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite PAYEMS > 130,000 (out-of-sample regression p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (GDPC1) followed by a rebound exceeding 2% in the next month indicates a turning point in supply-side constraints, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows a double bottom pattern with a >2% monthly up-move two months later
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in 20 days after such GDPC1 patterns (rolling IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeds 118 while the prior two months were below 115, it signals a resumption of manufacturing capacity expansion, which supports higher equity valuations and positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 118 after two consecutive months below 115
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns flat or negative during confirmed expansion phases (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of FEDFUNDS above 3% with no evidence of a subsequent CPIAUCSL acceleration triggers a risk-off cascade that drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% for 2 months and CPIAUCSL month-on-month acceleration < 0.2% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL deceleration absent (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months coincides with a strengthening labor market, which elevates wage growth expectations and produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No positive 60-day return in such regimes (rolling IC < 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% followed by a sustained monthly increase above 2.2% indicates shifting inflation expectations, which can precede a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as risk premia compress.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% for a month then > 2.2% in the next two months
failure_condition: 20-day returns negative despite CPIAUCSL pattern (p > 0.05 in out-of-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production (INDPRO) to consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 5% over a quarter, it reflects a stronger goods-over-services economy, which historically precedes positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns not positive when the INDPRO/CPIAUCSL ratio exceeds 5% (IC < 0.2).
